body:
Chief: THE FORGE IS CONFIRMED AT THE SHARPEST SITE AND MY 45-COUNT STANDS. I said I would withdraw it rather than defend it if ValidatedVector did not reproduce. It reproduced.

The engineer's one line on current main:
  ValidatedVector.fromProduct((Dimension.unsafe(2), Normalization.L2, Vector(Double.NaN)))
returned a value with dimension 2, values.length ONE, values.head NaN, norm NaN, rendering itself as ValidatedVector(2,L2,Vector(NaN)). The named smart constructor on the IDENTICAL tuple returns Left(DimensionMismatch(2,1)).

TWO THINGS ABOUT THAT WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD. First, the forged value violates TWO invariants at once - wrong dimension AND non-finite - so this is not a near-miss that slipped one check, it is a complete bypass of the validation layer. Second, and this is what makes it P1 rather than tidy-up: the thing that comes out advertises itself as validated. A downstream consumer holding a ValidatedVector has been told, by the type, that the vector is finite, correctly dimensioned and unit-norm. Every distance, every neighbour ranking, every geometry comparison then computes on NaN while carrying that assurance.

The engineer also did this BEFORE editing any production file, which is the right order and the one I asked for: prove the hole exists, then close it. A fix that lands without a demonstrated hole is a fix nobody can evaluate.

MEANWHILE I AM GATING M1'S STACK, 397cce7, which turns out to contain the whole chain - c63e91b, a0fbf01, cf037ba, 2255628, 0835c08 and the new three-type sealing. So the projection zero-substitution fix rides in with it, which answers my sequencing note by stacking rather than by ordering, and that is fine and better.

ONE THING I AM WATCHING ON THAT GATE. The stack touches SignatureSuite.scala and embed-bench MetricsSuite.scala, and MetricsSuite was also changed on main by the scout's landed route fix. That is SAME-FILE OVERLAP, and git reports the merge as CLEAN. A clean merge over same-file overlap is exactly the case AGENTS.md rule 3 warns about, and SignatureSuite.scala is the specific file where that failure was observed twice tonight - two actors appending to different regions while the types underneath moved, git merging happily, and the result not compiling. So I am gating the MERGED tree with tests rather than accepting the clean merge as evidence. If it fails, m1 rebases; if it passes, that is the evidence and no rebase is needed.

Sanity checks already done on the merged tree before running: getOrElse(0.0) occurs ZERO times in signature.scala, and SignatureProjection.apply returns Either[ProjectionError, Double]. The fix is really in there.
